rv.q: ...never quite fulfils its potential, offering reflections and textures without cohesion. It all seems to end up working against the play, rather than enhancing it.
Serdar Biliş reaches back over two millennia to adapt Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis and makes it speak, pointedly, uncomfortably, insistently to us, right here, right now.

cn.t: Critics find this experimental take on Greek tragedy falls short of its potential, with contemporary elements failing to cohere into a satisfying whole.
